warnings.headline: Storm Boelo will bring a very windy and wet spell this weekend with some disruption likely across parts of northern UK. : UPDATED
warnings.description:
Information on update: Warning extended further south across northern England and into north Wales. . Strong winds will spread across northern parts of the UK during Saturday afternoon, combining with spells of heavy rain. Initially strong southerly winds will affect parts of Scotland before more widespread and even stronger westerly winds develop later on Saturday. Very windy conditions will then persist overnight and through much of Sunday before gradually easing from the southwest later. Gusts of 55-65 mph are likely widely with some coastal and exposed areas potentially seeing gusts of 70-80 mph or more, these strongest gusts most likely across Scotland and the far north of England.

warnings.headline: Heavy rain associated with Storm Boelo is likely to cause some travel disruption and flooding in a few places
warnings.description:
Frequent heavy showers or more organised bands of rain will develop across northern Scotland during Saturday evening in association with Storm Boelo, continuing through Sunday morning and early afternoon. 

Accumulations of 20-40 mm are expected widely within the warning area through this period, with 60-80 mm possible in some locations, bringing flooding and travel disruption in a few places. Showers will become less frequent later through Sunday afternoon.

For further details see https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/weather/warnings-and-advice/uk-warnings

warnings.headline: A period of strong winds may lead to damaging gusts and transport disruption.
warnings.description:
Strong west to southwesterly winds are expected to spread across much of Scotland, the north of Northern Ireland and northern England on Tuesday. Gusts of 50-60 mph are possible quite widely and some coastal or exposed areas could see gusts of 70 mph or more, but at this time there is some uncertainty in where, and how strong, the peak gusts will be. The strongest of the winds will reduce from the southwest later on Tuesday, with the far north of Scotland the last to see winds ease.



For further details see https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/weather/warnings-and-advice/uk-warnings

warnings.event: Flood Warning: Cumbrian coastline from Gretna to Silloth including Port Carlisle, Skinburness and Rockcliffe
warnings.headline: Flooding is expected: Cumbrian coastline from Gretna to Silloth including Port Carlisle, Skinburness and Rockcliffe
warnings.description:
High tides, strong winds and large waves are expected to cause flooding this evening. 

Flooding is expected from 21:00PM on 24/10/2026 to 01:00AM on 25/10/2026. 

Flooding is possible due to high tides and strong winds from Storm Boelo. Locations most affected will be the Cumbrian coastline from Gretna to Silloth, areas at risk include  Rockcliffe, Longburgh, Port Carlisle, Bowness-on-Solway, Anthorn, Angerton and Skinburness areas. 

We are closely monitoring the situation and have closed the flood gates at Skinburness Marsh. 

Avoid seafronts and harbours due to wave overtopping and spray containing debris.  

This message will be updated by 9:00AM on Sunday 25 October or as the situation
